Each tuple in the list represents an edge, in the bipartite graph. 
The first element a_i of the tuple is the "source" of the edge, while the second element b_i is the "target". 
The third element c_i is the size of the data transferred from source a_i to target b_i, while the fourth element d_i is the size of the data transferred from target b_i to source a_i.
Suppose the source is at vertex 1 of the graph, target is at vertex 2, and the data transferred is 3 in both directions.

The bandwidth cost is the sum of the cost of the edges that touch the source, the edges that touch the target, and the edges that touch both, but not both twice.

You can think of the bandwidth cost as the number of times data flows from one node to another in the bipartite graph.
